plain.text: Jesus went back to his hometown, Nazareth, and taught in the synagogue. People were amazed, but also offended. "Isn't this the carpenter, Mary's son? Aren't his brothers and sisters here with us?" Jesus said, "A prophet is honoured everywhere except in his hometown and his own house." He could not do many miracles there, except heal a few sick people, and he was amazed at their lack of faith.

Jesus sent out the twelve in pairs and gave them authority over evil spirits. They were to take nothing for the journey but a staff: no bread, no bag, no money. If a place would not welcome them, they were to shake the dust off their feet as a warning. They went out and preached that people should turn from their sins. They drove out many demons and healed many sick people, anointing them with oil.

King Herod heard about Jesus and thought John the Baptist had come back from the dead. Herod had earlier arrested John, because John had told him it was wrong to marry his brother's wife, Herodias. Herodias wanted John killed. At Herod's birthday party, her daughter danced and pleased Herod, who promised her anything. Prompted by her mother, she asked for John's head on a platter. Herod was very sorry, but because of his promise in front of his guests, he had John beheaded. John's disciples buried his body.

The apostles came back and told Jesus all they had done. He said, "Come away with me to a quiet place and rest." But crowds followed them. Jesus had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he taught them. Late in the day, there was nothing to eat. The disciples had only five loaves and two fish. Jesus had the people sit in groups, looked up to heaven, gave thanks and broke the bread. Everyone ate and was satisfied, and they picked up twelve baskets of leftovers. About five thousand men had eaten.

Jesus sent the disciples across the lake while he went up a mountain to pray. In the night, he saw them struggling against the wind. He came to them, walking on the water. They thought he was a ghost and were terrified. He said, "Take courage! It is I. Don't be afraid." He climbed into the boat and the wind stopped. They were amazed, because their hearts had not yet understood the miracle of the loaves.
When they landed at Gennesaret, people recognised Jesus and brought sick people to him wherever he went. They begged to touch even the edge of his cloak, and all who touched it were healed.

summary.bigIdea: Jesus provides, protects and has compassion, even when people doubt him.
points: Jesus is rejected in his hometown, and sends his disciples out to share his work.
John the Baptist dies for speaking the truth to a king.
Jesus feeds five thousand people and walks on water: "Take courage! It is I."
summary.reflection: Jesus saw the crowd as sheep without a shepherd and had compassion. Where do you need his care right now?
